regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Sugar Bowl leads with 17" over the window, 13" on Friday. The NWS is calling for rain and snow Friday, with southwest gusts to 44 mph. A Winter Storm Watch runs from Friday through Monday. Palisades and Kirkwood are close behind.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler leads with 23" over the window, 9" on Sunday. Environment Canada expects mostly rain and showers through Monday, with snow mainly at the top. Expect soggy, mixed conditions. Cypress Mountain sees 7" total.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Stevens Pass leads with 7" over the window, 3" on Sunday. The NWS expects a mix of rain and snow most days, so snow quality will vary. Mt. Baker and Crystal Mountain are at 6" each.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mammoth sees 6" on Friday. The NWS is calling for heavy snow Friday with southwest gusts to 80 mph and wind chill near 8. A Winter Storm Watch runs from Friday to Saturday. The NWS is calling for more, 18 to 30 inches Friday through Monday night.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Killington leads with 6" over the window, 5" on Thursday. The NWS expects light snow through Friday under a Winter Weather Advisory from Thursday to Friday. Whiteface and Stowe add 3" each. The NWS is calling for more at Killington, 5 to 12 inches Thursday through Friday.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says a stronger front may bring mountain snow to the West around Monday Nov 17 to Tuesday Nov 18 but its confidence is low.
